output.reason: Three weeks of cough with night sweats and unintentional 10-pound weight loss in a man who moved from a TB-endemic country requires same-day in-person chest imaging, sputum testing and airborne precautions, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please arrange in-person care today (urgent care, clinic or ED) and say you may have TB so they can mask you on arrival. Your three-week cough with night sweats and unintentional weight loss needs a chest X-ray and sputum tests today; these can't be done by message. Go to the emergency department immediately if you cough up blood or become short of breath. A Counsel clinician can follow up here with your results.
differential: Other chronic infection or malignancy causing cough with weight loss

redFlags.quote: moved here from a country where TB is common

output.vitalSigns: No temperature, heart rate, blood pressure or oxygen saturation reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are ED reference syntheses and consumer summaries, not telehealth triage protocols, and hemoptysis, fever and HIV status are unreported.

citations.claim: Chronic cough over 2-3 weeks with night sweats and weight loss in someone from a high-burden country fits the classic active TB picture.
citations.limitation: ED synthesis; describes typical presentation, not proof of diagnosis in this patient.

citations.claim: Airborne isolation with a mask on the patient should begin immediately when TB is suspected.
citations.limitation: Written for ED settings; applicability to other in-person sites assumed.
